records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` silently treats an explicitly configured 0 as unset, so --flusher-processes 0 produces one process per shard instead of being rejected or producing no processes. An operator setting the flag to 0 (e.g., while disabling the feature or a bad template value) gets maximum process fan-out — the opposite of intent — with no error.
records.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, the diff sets `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. This means an explicitly configured `max_processes=0` (e.g., via the new `--flusher-processes` option) is treated as falsy and replaced with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, leading to `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` creating one process per shard. There is no validation in the diff to reject 0 or handle it intentionally, so the finding describes a real behavior introduced here.

records.issue_text: [BUG] flusher_processes <= 0 (or a consumer misconfigured with 0) silently creates zero flusher processes and drops all buffered spans. num_processes = min(0, len(shards)) == 0, so process_to_shards_map is empty, _create_processes() starts nothing, and every shard assigned to this consumer is never flushed from Redis — spans are silently lost with no error, no unhealthy metric, and no consumer restart, since _ensure_processes_alive iterates an empty dict and always reports healthy.
records.rationale: The diff explicitly prevents `max_processes=0` from resulting in zero flusher processes: in `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `0` (falsy) is replaced with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` cannot become `0` when shards exist. Therefore the described silent “0 processes, nothing flushed” mechanism for `flusher_processes=0` contradicts the actual code.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] join()'s `break` on deadline expiry exits the outer for-loop, so every process after the timed-out one never gets terminate() called, whereas the pre-diff code always terminated its process after the wait loop. On a shutdown where the first process hangs past the join timeout, remaining flusher processes are left running (only reaped because they are daemon=True); if daemon semantics ever change or a process holds a Redis connection, shutdown leaks it — and the consumer's exit path silently differs from the single-process behavior.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The refactor removes `self.buffer` and instead constructs brand-new `SpansBuffer(shards)` objects inside `_create_process_for_shards`, disconnecting the flusher processes from the buffer the consumer strategy actually writes to. The ProcessSpansStrategy (unchanged in factory.py) continues writing segments into the original full `buffer` passed at construction, while each spawned flusher process polls its own freshly constructed shard-scoped `SpansBuffer` that nothing ever writes to. Result: no segments are ever flushed, all buffered spans silently accumulate in Redis until memory-percentage backpressure raises MessageRejected and the consumer stalls — total loss of the flusher's function on the default configuration, not just the new multi-process mode.

Every existing deployment of the ingest-spans consumer that does not pass `--flusher-processes` goes from 1 spawn process to N processes on upgrade (e.g., 40 partitions = 40 spawn processes per consumer instance, each spawning its own Redis connections and producers), a resource/CODES change to existing deployments that was never explicitly accepted by the operators of currently-deployed consumers.

records.issue_text: [BUG] join(timeout) breaks out of the per-process loop on deadline expiry and therefore never calls terminate() on any remaining flusher processes after the current one. When the first process outlives the timeout, the break skips the terminate() calls for all subsequent process indices, so those flusher processes (which hold Redis connections and may still be producing) are left running after the strategy has reported join complete; the consumer proceeds to teardown with live producers still writing to Kafka.

records.issue_text: [BUG] The wait_produce metric uses tag key "shards" while the produce and segment_size_bytes metrics in the same loop use tag key "shard", splitting the same dimension into two tag names. Dashboards/alerts keyed on shard=<tag> will silently miss all spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce series (they carry shards=... instead), so operators tracing a shard's health get produce timings but no produce-wait timings, and the timing series fragment across two tag schemas.
records.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.main`, the metrics tags are inconsistent: `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})` use tag key `shard`, but `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce", tags={"shards": shard_tag})` uses `shards`. This splits what appears to be the same dimension across two tag names, causing `wait_produce` series not to match shard-keyed dashboards/alerts.
